To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the food stamp program reaches about half of eligible households; (b) the program reaches a higher percentage of the very poor than of the near poor; (c) there is a strong negative relationship between the level of participation in the program and income; and (d) the program reaches more of the elderly poor than of the non-elderly poor. 2 See, for example, Rainwater (1970) and Piven and Cloward (1971) for discussions
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why eligible households do not participate in public transfer welfare programs.
the extent to which households eligible for food stamps actually participate in the program.
the question of why eligible households do not receive food stamps.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence on the nonparticipation in the food stamp program is mixed, and that there are no definitive answers as to the extent of nonparticipation and why it occurs.
nonparticipation rates are high for most welfare programs and are particularly high in the case of the Food Stamp program.
the food stamp program is an effective and efficient means of transferring income to low income households.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a large number of eligible households not participating in the food stamp program.
the welfare system is not as efficient as it should be, and that the problem of nonparticipation is a serious one.
there was no evidence of any significant change in the participation rates of eligible households in the food stamp program between 1975 and 1977.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lot of room for improvement in the way we measure the performance of the U.S. economy, and in the way we use the data to inform economic policymaking.
there are many households that are eligible for food stamps but are not receiving them.
the Food Stamps program is not reaching a substantial portion of eligible households.
